newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government approves plan on budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian government approves plan on budget cuts.

text.p: The Russian government has approved a plan to cut spending in its 1997 budget, necessitated by a significant shortfall of expected revenue, a government spokeswoman said on Friday.
Details of the plan, which must be approved by parliament, were not immediately released.
Last week, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said that revenues in the first quarter were only 57 percent of budgeted levels.
As a result the goverment is unable to meet many of its funding obligations, ranging from Russia's space programme to paying salaries of tax inspectors and other state workers.
The spokeswoman said the government had agreed in principle to a Finance Ministry proposal to cut spending in line with lower than expected revenues.

Under the 1997 budget law, if revenues in any quarter are less than 90 percent of planned the government must present a bill to the State Duma (lower house of parliament) on "sequestering", or cutting spending.
The spending cuts have to win approval in parliament, dominated by communists and conservatives.
Many deputies have already said they will not allow the government to reduce budget support for items such as hospitals and social payments.
President Boris Yeltsin signed the 1997 budget in late February.
